# Agreed fourth-highest opening lead: preregistered protocol

**Prediction.** A communicated rank constraint may improve defensive agreement even when an uncommunicated lead tie convention cannot.
The sender-only contrast estimates the cost or benefit of the lead itself, the receiver contrast estimates the additional effect of using the rank message, and the package contrast measures the net result.
This is a study of fixed partnership agreements, not a production change or promotion decision.

**Population and arms.** Use 48 fresh full, unpassed 3NT deals, generated by `makeBoard(7910000+i, 1+5*i, 0)` for zero-based `i` (cycle dealer and vulnerability).
Both partnerships get the incumbent search when declaring.
When defending: (I) incumbent, (S) same policy except the opening leader always plays fourth-highest from a longest suit, breaking length ties by `SUITS`, with no DDS override, (D) same sender as S plus the leader's partner conditions on exactly three original higher cards of the opening suit belonging to the leader, including those already played by the leader.
No other inference about length, ranks, or seat is communicated.
No agreed policy can start from a prefix or suit contract.

**Search and pairing.** Incumbent DDS card ranking (IMP utility against making 3NT exactly, then expected duplicate score, then low rank; stable legal order on remaining ties).
Use three IID layouts with replacement at every searched decision, no exact enumeration and no timing-based truncation.
Forced one-card plays and the fixed opening lead need no samples.
Singleton layout distributions are sampled three times as required.
Each arm gets the same random stream initialization by deal, ply and seat, using `seed ^ imul(ply*4+seatIndex+1, 0x9e3779b9)` and the arena PRNG.
Rejection consumes additional draws on that decision's stream only; cap at 4,096 proposals for each requested layout and record any failure without fallback.
Unconditional proposals use the incumbent visible-card sampler.
The only added condition applies to the true partner of the opening leader in D, never the leader, declarer/dummy, random prefixes, or unagreed leads.

Each board supplies one two-table result per contrast with swapped candidate partnerships, same deal and common action streams.
Since declarer always uses incumbent, the two tables for a contrast are just its two defender arms, and shared tables are evaluated once.
Calculate candidate-minus-control NS scores when the candidate defends NS, and control-minus-candidate NS scores otherwise, then convert to IMPs.
Record every board's three paired IMPs (S−I, D−S, D−I), NS scores, searched decisions, proposals and DDS calls, and any exceptional failure (missing contrast as `null`, retained in the denominator).
Report wins/ties/losses, totals and means, and descriptive uncertainty at the board level via the existing one-sided bootstrap lower bound.
Failure makes any affected mean unavailable for the full sample and blocks the gate; no board substitutions or exclusions.

**Decision rule.** Only if D−I AND D−S each have strictly positive aggregate IMPs and strictly more wins than losses, with no failures, run 128 fresh deals beginning at seed 8010000 with the same board numbering, arms and settings.
Confirm both on that independent set using the same two requirements; report all three contrasts regardless.
Descriptive intervals do not change the gate.
No live promotion even if confirmed.
No retuning, stopping early, or alternative selection based on these outcomes.

**Checks before scoring.** Run the focused tests first against the pre-implementation state to establish the red result, then against the implementation.
Check incumbent decisions against `analyzePlay` on separate development deals; independently enumerate a small legal-world fixture from original ownership and historical follow-suit; check rank conditioning support, the already-played ranks, gating and the tied-longest lead.
Reproduction: `node --import tsx scripts/self-play/agreed-lead.ts`.

## Pre-run checks

The focused test file was run before the implementation existed (red: missing study module).
Separately, on development seed 1736, board 1, the incumbent chose C2 at the opening lead with three layouts and search seed 0, whereas the specified lead was S6.
After implementation and before the screen, the four focused tests passed: lead selection, seat/arm and prefix gating, independently replayed small-world conditional support and the rejection cap, and incumbent choices on eight development positions.
Final integration repeated the incumbent comparison on 24 positions from three development deals (seeds 1736–1738), with no disagreements.
The final two-file typecheck and four focused tests passed.

## Screen results

All 48 deals completed, with no table or sampling failures.
The screen ran on Linux x64 with Node 22.22.1 and bridge-dds 1.4.0.
The measured evaluator's SHA-256 before final source formatting was `b5e3815f6b469a7a0751cfdc01a12837696def175150ea4ecb49adefe96be170`.

| Paired contrast | Wins–ties–losses | Total IMPs | IMPs/deal | One-sided 95% bootstrap lower bound |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sender only − incumbent | 11–26–11 | +13 | +0.271 | −0.938 |
| Decoder − sender only | 13–22–13 | −21 | −0.438 | −1.542 |
| Package − incumbent | 17–15–16 | −5 | −0.104 | −1.375 |

The sender-only arm had a small positive observed score but equal wins and losses, so this does not establish a benefit from the lead alone.
The estimated receiver effect was negative with equal wins and losses; the package won one more board than it lost, but was negative in aggregate IMPs.
The prediction did not receive support in this screen; the bounds do not establish harm either.
Both required contrasts missed the gate, so the 128-board confirmation was not run and nothing was promoted to live.
Each contrast was converted to IMPs separately from duplicate-score differences; the IMP contrasts are not additive.

| Defender arm | Searched decisions | Conditioned decisions | Proposed layouts | DDS calls | Table failures |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Incumbent | 1,968 | 0 | 5,904 | 5,904 | 0 |
| Sender only | 1,916 | 0 | 5,748 | 5,748 | 0 |
| Sender and decoder | 1,931 | 493 | 8,546 | 5,793 | 0 |

The decoder rejected 2,753 proposals while accepting 1,479 conditional layouts.
[Raw JSONL](agreed-lead.jsonl) contains all 48 boards followed by the phase summary and gate decision.
Its `score` and `work` arrays are in I, S, D order, with each work tuple containing searched decisions, conditioned decisions, proposals, and DDS calls.
The `imps` array is S−I, D−S, D−I.
The raw rows were independently checked against the duplicate IMP thresholds, scheduled board and seed sequence, and three-layout work invariant.
